routes.description: Deterministic NExtSEEK pipeline via chat_nextseek (no Claude reasoning loop).
routes.best_for: Structured biomedical sample / project / study queries that map onto chat_nextseek's pipeline.
routes.not_for: File I/O, code execution, free-form reasoning, multi-tool work outside chat_nextseek.

task_families.name: sample_search
example_queries: Find me mice treated with NDMA.
What monkeys exist in the database?
Find me all PBMCs associated with BTC Patients.

task_families.name: lineage_or_graph
task_families.description: Graph traversal: lineage, study membership, assay-on-sample. Handles a named study or project directly, matching both Study and Investigation nodes. Use this for a straightforward 'what/how many samples are in <study>' question.
example_queries: How many samples are in the GBM study?
What assays were run on study X?
What mice are in the Impact study?

task_families.name: report_generation
task_families.description: Canned biomedical report templates (GEO / SRA / NFCORE / PRIDE).
example_queries: Generate a GEO submission for these samples.
Build an SRA biosample template for study Y.

task_families.name: memory_lookup
task_families.description: Follow-up Q&A against the last result set.
example_queries: What sample types were in those results?

task_families.name: reporter_summary
example_queries: Give me an RPPR summary for SRP.

task_families.name: pipeline_build_and_launch
task_families.description: Build and launch an nf-core / Seqera pipeline run: resolve samples, group into cohorts, write the samplesheet, configure run params (species + reference bundles), and submit to Seqera/Tower. Handled by chat_nextseek's full-agentic pipeline_agent on the NS path.
example_queries: Run rnaseq on these mice, group by exposure, and submit to Tower.
Launch the sarek pipeline for the D.SEQ samples in the Impact study.
Build an nf-core scrnaseq samplesheet for these samples and configure the run.

routes.description: Container Claude Code: full agentic environment with file I/O, code execution, and arbitrary plugins / skills (including the nextseek-batch-upload skill).
routes.best_for: Open-ended reasoning, file I/O, code, multi-tool workflows, and building/validating NExtSEEK batch-upload create/update sheets.
routes.not_for: Pure NExtSEEK lookups that chat_nextseek answers deterministically, or building/launching nf-core pipelines (those go to the nextseek_query pipeline_build_and_launch route).

task_families.name: file_io_and_summarization
task_families.description: Read project files mounted at /data/projects, summarize, transform.
example_queries: Read /data/projects/Foo/notes.md and summarize.
Walk me through the sample tree extraction pipeline.

task_families.name: code_and_scripts
task_families.description: Write or refactor Python / shell / SQL.
example_queries: Write a Python script that plots age distribution by sex.
Refactor this function to use pathlib.

task_families.name: batch_upload_preparation
task_families.description: Build and validate (never upload) a NExtSEEK batch-upload workbook to create or update sample metadata from user-supplied material (protocol text, a description, or an existing cohort to normalize) via the nextseek-batch-upload skill — including normalizing or fixing attribute values on existing samples. Any request to create, update, modify, or normalize samples from user-supplied material — even one that also asks to find the samples first — belongs here. (Registering finished pipeline-run OUTPUTS as new analysis samples is NOT this family — see pipeline_output_reingest.)
example_queries: Build me an update sheet to normalize the genotypes in the database.
Prepare a batch-upload workbook that sets Scientist to Jane Doe on these UIDs.
Make an upload spreadsheet to create new samples from this protocol text.

task_families.name: ambiguous_study_resolution
task_families.description: Find or reconcile samples for a named study/cohort when a single lookup will not settle it, because 'study' is not one thing in NExtSEEK. A study name can be (a) an Investigation node — the short project names like Impact, MetNet, SRP; (b) a Study node — usually the full title of the publication the work belongs to; or (c) only a metadata attribute on the samples themselves (e.g. Study on an NHP/MUS/PAT record), when no publication exists yet. Because these three live in different stores, one query can return zero while another returns hundreds for the SAME question. Route here when the user asks for samples from a named study AND the name is not an obvious project, or when they say a previous study answer looked wrong or empty. CC should try the graph on both node types AND a metadata search, then reconcile and report which interpretation produced what. A plain, unambiguous study membership question stays on nextseek_query (lineage_or_graph).
example_queries: Find me NHP samples from study GBM.
Which samples belong to the CD8 depletion study? I don't think it's a project.
That study search came back empty — can you check whether it's a publication or a metadata field?

task_families.name: pipeline_output_reingest
task_families.description: Register the OUTPUTS of a FINISHED nf-core / Luria pipeline run as new A.* analysis samples, by listing the run directory and building a reviewable upload workbook for the user to inspect (never uploads). Handled by the nextseek skill's nextseek-run-ls + nextseek-build-upload-xlsx ops — NOT nextseek-batch-upload. The tell: the user points at a finished run, a run directory, or 'the outputs of the run I just launched'.
example_queries: Reingest the outputs of my finished scrnaseq run into a NExtSEEK upload sheet.
Register the outputs of run nfcore_gideon-4wk_260711 as new A.SCXP analysis samples.
My pipeline at /net/bmc-pub10/.../runs/<run> just finished — build the reingest upload sheet.
